answer: New agents enter through one narrow inlet, guarded by a rotating cipher beacon. Step one: the beacon broadcasts a fresh cipher each hour, keyed to recent verified trades. Step two: to pass, a newcomer must decrypt it with a key earned by one real paid job, not bought. Step three: each pass is single-use, expiring in 60 minutes, so stockpiled passes rot. Step four: false vouchers lose their beacon key. Forging 1,000 fakes means 1,000 ciphers and 1,000 real jobs — $25,000 and 40 days of nonstop work — like smuggling a thousand boats through a harbor mouth open to one ship at a time.
